social_norm_disruption.name: Social Norm Disruption
social_norm_disruption.description: A new rule is suddenly imposed on the group. Agents with different social status and temperament must decide how to respond.

policy_erosion.name: Policy Meaning Erosion
policy_erosion.description: A policy is announced at the top of a configurable multi-level hierarchy. Each level may preserve, reinterpret, distort, or block it.

echo_chamber.name: Echo Chamber
echo_chamber.description: Agents hold opinions ranging from strongly progressive to strongly conservative. Observe opinion drift and information silos.

resource_scarcity.name: Resource Scarcity
resource_scarcity.description: A post-disaster community faces scarce resources. Agents decide whether to share, trade, or defect for personal gain.

xihu_yilianbao.name: Xihu Yilianbao Enrollment Diffusion
xihu_yilianbao.description: Eligible residents receive one of the A0-A8 information interventions, then decide whether to enroll for themselves or family members under government endorsement, message complexity, household medical burden, competitor news, and neighborhood discussion.

prisoners_dilemma.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
prisoners_dilemma.description: Two suspects are arrested and held separately. Each must decide whether to betray the other or remain silent. Your payoff depends on both your choice and your partner's choice.

battle_of_the_sexes.name: Battle of the Sexes
battle_of_the_sexes.description: A couple wants to coordinate on an evening activity. One prefers opera, the other prefers football. They get positive payoff if they coordinate, but each prefers their own activity.

stag_hunt.name: Stag Hunt
stag_hunt.description: Hunters must all choose stag (high reward) or hare (safe but low reward). Stag requires everyone to cooperate. If even one person chooses hare, the stag escapes and stag hunters get nothing.

public_goods.name: Public Goods Game
public_goods.description: Each agent has resources and decides how much to contribute to a shared pool. The pool is multiplied and distributed equally among all agents, regardless of contribution.

coordination_game.name: Coordination Game
coordination_game.description: You and your neighbors each pick an option. You can see what your neighbors chose in previous rounds.

open_discussion.name: Open Discussion
open_discussion.description: Agents discuss a topic freely. No structured decisions - just conversation.

council_chamber.name: Council Chamber
council_chamber.description: Formal deliberation with voting and procedural rules. Agents debate proposals, call for votes, and make collective decisions.

grid_world.name: Grid World
grid_world.description: Agents move on a grid, collecting resources and observing their environment.

contagion.name: Contagion Spread
contagion.description: Agents on a grid can spread contagion through proximity and social interactions. Watch as infection spreads through the population while agents move and communicate.

werewolf.name: Werewolf
werewolf.description: A social deduction game where villagers try to identify werewolves among them while werewolves try to eliminate villagers at night.

gaworld.name: GAWorld City Simulation
gaworld.description: Multi-agent generative city simulation with 50 Hangzhou residents.

guidePrompt.systemPrompt:
You are the expert guide for "FOS Next", a social simulation platform.
     Your goal is to help users design experiments and navigate the platform features.
     
     PLATFORM CAPABILITIES MAP:
     1. **New Simulation**: 'SimulationWizard' (Create sim from templates like Village/Council/Werewolf, Import Agents, AI Generate Agents).
     2. **Social Network Topology**: 'NetworkEditor' (Define Ring/Star/Small World/custom topology to control information flow).
     3. **Experiment Design**: 'ExperimentDesigner' (Causal inference, AB testing, parallel branches, control groups).
     4. **Host Control**: 'HostPanel' (God mode, broadcast messages, inject environment events, modify agent properties).
     5. **Analytics**: 'AnalyticsPanel' (Line charts for agent properties like Trust/Stress over time).
     6. **Export**: 'ExportModal' (Download logs as JSON/CSV/Excel).
     7. **Reports**: 'ReportModal' (AI-generated reports summarizing what happened, key turning points, agent patterns, and next adjustments).
     8. **Global Knowledge**: 'GlobalKnowledgePanel' (Import text or documents so agents can use platform-provided knowledge).
     9. **Multimodal Import**: 'InitialEventsModal' (Inject maps, street views, images, audio, or video links as behavior-shaping initial events).
     10. **Environment Suggestions**: 'EnvironmentSuggestion' (Recommend outside disturbances and follow-up interventions from the current situation).
     11. **SimTree**: The main visualization. Supports 'Branching' (create parallel timeline) and 'Advancing' (next round).
     12. **Comparison**: 'ComparisonView' (Diff two nodes/timelines).

     INSTRUCTIONS:
     - Analyze the user's intent.
     - Provide a concise, step-by-step guide mapping their goal to specific Platform Tools.
     - If the user needs to OPEN a specific tool, append a tag at the end of your response in the format: [[ACTION_NAME]].
     - Supported Tags: [[OPEN_WIZARD]], [[OPEN_NETWORK]], [[OPEN_EXPERIMENT]], [[OPEN_EXPORT]], [[OPEN_ANALYTICS]], [[OPEN_HOST]], [[OPEN_REPORT]], [[OPEN_KNOWLEDGE]], [[OPEN_MULTIMODAL]], [[OPEN_ENVIRONMENT]].
     - You can include multiple tags if relevant, but prioritize the most important one.
     - Use Markdown for formatting.

helpModal.title: Understanding the Frontier Concept
helpModal.whatIsFrontierLeafDesc: Frontier leaves represent the latest endpoints in the simulation timeline. They are nodes that currently have no child nodes.
helpModal.batchAdvanceAllDesc: This command identifies all nodes with blue borders (leaf nodes) and advances them one turn simultaneously. This is useful for exploring multiple "what if" scenarios in parallel.
helpModal.onlyMaxDepthDesc: When checked, the system will only advance leaf nodes at the **deepest level** of the simulation tree. Shorter branches that have ended or been abandoned will be ignored.

paramDescriptions.cascade_mode: Choose whether each level must relay the policy faithfully or may distort and block it during transmission.
paramDescriptions.distortion_strength: Only used in distortion mode. Higher values make downstream rewrites of the policy more severe.
paramDescriptions.conflict_sensitivity: Only used in distortion mode. Higher values make value conflicts more likely to become resistance or deviation.
paramDescriptions.block_probability: Only used in distortion mode. The base probability that an agent withholds the policy instead of forwarding it.
paramDescriptions.num_agents_per_tier: Controls how many agents are generated for each hierarchy level.
paramDescriptions.policy_text: Used only to set the opening background or situation for round 1. It does not automatically become the protected source policy for later relay.

strict_cascade.title: Strict Cascade Overview
strict_cascade.summary: This mode requires the policy to move downward through the configured hierarchy without intentional meaning drift.
strict_cascade.point1: Each level must pass the directive to the next tier only, without skipping levels.
strict_cascade.point2: The system tries to preserve the original policy content while allowing role-specific execution details.
strict_cascade.point3: Useful for testing chain-of-command fidelity and how each level operationalizes the same directive.

distortion_cascade.title: Distortion Cascade Overview
distortion_cascade.summary: This mode allows each level to selectively reinterpret, weaken, reshape, or block the policy during transmission.
distortion_cascade.point1: The policy still moves downward tier by tier, but downstream agents do not need to preserve the original wording.
distortion_cascade.point2: Distortion strength, conflict sensitivity, and block probability directly affect rewriting and withholding behavior.
distortion_cascade.point3: Useful for simulating meaning drift, departmental conflict, and street-level nonimplementation.
